newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares ease with no upswing in sight.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares ease with no upswing in sight.

text.p: The Nigerian stock market's all-share index fell again on Friday on persistent bearish trade and dealers said an upswing was not in the horizon for sometime.
It closed at 8329.18 on Friday from 8350.91 on Thursday.
Dealers said the market remained in the grips of heavy selling by cash-starved investors and others moving funds to a more attractive money market.
"It matches what happened about three months ago when the stocks were galloping and people were screaming that this was unsustainable," one trader said.
That was when interest rates crashed, forcing a diversion into equities. Growing demand for shares then pushed prices up by big margins.
"It is a reverse flow we are experiencing now that money market rates have fallen and funds have started moving there again," the trader said.
Dealers said the market was still on the downswing in the immediate future as large volumes of shares were on offer.
"Many investors are rushing to sell, believing the stocks would fall more," one said.
Worst hit were conglomerates and oil marketers whose prices had appreciated considerably earlier in the year.
Unipetrol was down 50 kobo on Friday at 65.00 naira while African Petroleum, at 52.70 naira, and Total TOTL.LG, at 56.20 naira, lost 20 kobo apiece.
Lever Bothers and Nestle both closed 20 kobo down at 25.80 naira and 51.50 naira, respectively.
West African Portland Cement Company (WAPCO) slid by 15 kobo to 60.50 naira. It was trailed by Ashaka Cement which dropped 10 kobo at 12.60 naira.
First Bank was the sector's biggest loser, finishing 10 kobo down at 12.70 naira.
But impressive dealers rewarded AIICO Insurance with full marks upon receiving its 1996 financial result.
The company said after-tax profit rose to 68.2 million naira against 36 million naira a year earlier.
It would pay no dividend but proposed a one-for-one scrip issue, which traders welcomed by hiking its price by 70 kobo or the maximum five percent allowed daily to 14.70 naira.

Okomu Oil palm also finished strongly, rising 25 kobo to 12.80 naira while oil miller P.S. Mandrides continued its ascent on its favourable financial performance. It ended 10 kobo higher at 7.20 naira.
Newly-listed Co-operative Bank, still in limelight in its first week as a quoted firm, closed two kobo up at 1.08 naira.
Paint maker IPWA, just back from loss-making, climbed by five kobo to 1.78 naira.
